title: FATAL: Q-acyclicity of universal cover deduced via an invalid Zeeman/SS comparison (counterexample RP^2)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** `thm:main`, paragraph "Rational acyclicity of $\widetilde M$" (final step).

**The error.** The proof establishes that $c\colon M\to B\Gamma$ is a $\pi_1$-isomorphism and a $\mathbb{Q}$-homology isomorphism (this part is fine), then invokes the **Zeeman comparison theorem** on the ladder of Serre fibrations over $B\Gamma$ to deduce
$$\widetilde c_*\colon H_*(\widetilde M;\mathbb{Q})\xrightarrow{\cong}H_*(E\Gamma;\mathbb{Q})=H_*(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb{Q}),$$
i.e. $\widetilde M$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic.

**This inference is invalid.** Zeeman's comparison theorem requires a **simply connected base** (or trivial/nilpotent local coefficients). Here the base is $B\Gamma$ with $\Gamma$ **infinite**, and the $E^2$-terms are $H_p(\Gamma;H_q(\widetilde M;\mathbb{Q}))$ with $\Gamma$ acting **nontrivially** on the fiber homology (the deck action). The offered "hyperhomology/Tor" reformulation is equally invalid: from
$$\mathbb{Q}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}\Gamma}\widetilde c_\#\ \text{a quasi-iso}$$
one **cannot** conclude $\widetilde c_\#$ is a quasi-iso over $\mathbb{Q}\Gamma$ — $\mathbb{Q}\Gamma$ for infinite $\Gamma$ is not local, and Nakayama/descent fails.

**Counterexample to the rule used.** Take $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}/2$, $M=\mathbb{RP}^2$. Then $c\colon\mathbb{RP}^2\to B\mathbb{Z}/2$ is a $\pi_1$-iso and a $\mathbb{Q}$-homology iso ($H_*(\mathbb{RP}^2;\mathbb{Q})=\mathbb{Q}=H_*(B\mathbb{Z}/2;\mathbb{Q})$), yet the universal cover $\widetilde M=S^2$ is **not** $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic. The nontrivial action on $H_2(S^2;\mathbb{Q})$ by $-1$ makes the coinvariants vanish, so $H_*(M;\mathbb{Q})$ "hides" the fiber homology — exactly the mechanism the proof ignores.

**Consequence.** The argument for the *central conclusion of the whole paper* is wrong. The conclusion may still hold for the specific $\widetilde M$ constructed, but it must be proved by a **direct $\Gamma$-equivariant computation** of $H_*(\widetilde M;\mathbb{Q})$ (equivariant/proper Mayer–Vietoris over $\widetilde M=(X\setminus\Gamma\cdot\text{cones})\cup\Gamma\cdot\widetilde W_F$, using $X$ contractible, $V_F$ $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic rel boundary, links $\mathbb{Q}HS$), **not** by descent from $H_*(M;\mathbb{Q})$. (Open issue q7-12 asks for that direct computation; this issue flags that the *submitted* proof uses an invalid shortcut that must be removed.)

## Mathematical Review (critic-agent) — current `solution.tex`

I re-reviewed the present `solution.tex` against all prior docs and open issues. The
strategy (Weinberger-style equivariant rational resolution of the orbifold $X/\Gamma$) is
correct and the YES answer is very likely right, but **the proof is not correct as
written**. Full write-up linked as *Critic Analysis* (`questions/q7/analysis.md`). Summary
of findings, each verified against the current file:

### FATAL — q7-15 (Zeeman descent is invalid). STILL PRESENT.
In `thm:main`, paragraph "*Rational acyclicity of $\widetilde M$*", the proof correctly
shows $c\colon M\to B\Gamma$ is a $\pi_1$-iso and a $\mathbb{Q}$-homology iso, then invokes
the **Zeeman comparison theorem** over the base $B\Gamma$ to conclude
$H_*(\widetilde M;\mathbb{Q})\cong H_*(E\Gamma;\mathbb{Q})$. Zeeman requires a
**simply-connected base**; $B\Gamma$ is not (here $\Gamma$ is infinite and acts
nontrivially on fiber homology). The "Tor over $\mathbb{Q}\Gamma$" reformulation is also
invalid (no Nakayama descent for infinite $\Gamma$).

**Counterexample to the exact rule used** (numerically checked): $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}/2$,
$M=\mathbb{RP}^2$. Then $c\colon\mathbb{RP}^2\to B\mathbb{Z}/2$ is a $\pi_1$-iso and a
$\mathbb{Q}$-homology iso, but the universal cover $\widetilde M=S^2$ is **not**
$\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic (the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action on $H_2(S^2;\mathbb{Q})$ by $-1$ kills the
coinvariants, so base homology hides fiber homology). The conclusion must instead be proved
by a **direct $\Gamma$-equivariant Mayer–Vietoris** computation on $\widetilde M$ — exactly
**q7-12**. Drop the Zeeman step entirely.

### Structural gaps — all STILL PRESENT.
- **q7-16 (surgery framing):** `thm:atomic` Step 2/3 kills $H_i(V_0;\mathbb{Q})$ by surgery
  asserting the normal bundle is "stably trivial and hence trivial," but $V_0$ is an
  arbitrary null-bordism with **no normal-map data**; killing homology needs a *trivialized*
  normal bundle (degree-one normal map), not mere embeddability.
- **q7-17 (bundle of models):** $R_F:=W_F\times_{O(\nu)}P(\nu)$ requires $O(\nu)$ to
  **act on the fiber $W_F$**, extending the linear action on $\partial W_F=S(V)$. $W_F$ is
  built by non-canonical surgery; no such action exists, so $R_F$ is not constructed for
  $\dim C>0$ and `lem:tube` (Leray–Hirsch) does not get off the ground.
- **q7-18 (scope overstated):** unconditional only for all-$\mathbb{Z}/2$ free-slice
  isotropy. Larger $2$-group stabilizers give non-atomic links; the $N$-fold rational device
  produces $N$ disjoint copies, not a single filling with the correct boundary.
- **q7-19 (non-atomic boundary matching):** the resolved link $\widehat L$ (from
  `prop:induct`) is glued to the genuine frontier $S(\nu)$ without an explicit
  $F$-diffeomorphism; resolved boundary $\neq$ genuine frontier in general.

### Carry-over: q7-10 (∂W_F = S(V) equivariantly), q7-11 (π₁≅Γ — sound for atomic, depends
on q7-17/19 in non-atomic), q7-12 (the correct acyclicity route), q7-4 (local model, depends
on q7-16) remain open and unmet.

### Stale: q7-20, q7-21, q7-23 cite `thm:resolution` / `prop:lefschetz`, which **do not
appear** in the current `solution.tex` (0 occurrences). They pertain to an earlier variant
and are not applicable to the present file.

**Bottom line.** No new issues needed — the existing open issues fully and accurately
capture the genuine gaps. The single highest-leverage fix is to replace the broken Zeeman
descent (q7-15) with the direct equivariant Mayer–Vietoris computation (q7-12); after that,
close q7-16/17 to make the local model and its bundle rigorous, then either restrict scope
(q7-18) or supply the $2$-primary bordism input for non-atomic strata (q7-18/19).
